name: Datatime Bishkek KR Data Center (Data 5)
notes: First commercial Tier III* data centre in Kyrgyzstan, opened 2024-06; operator page (A) confirms 500 kW+ marketed capacity, Koytashsky lane 46/1, dual 6 kV city substations, 2x1 MW diesel generators, 800 kVA UPS, N+1 cooling; Uptime Institute lists Tier III Certification of Design Documents only (not constructed-facility/operations certification); DCD trade press (B) confirms launch and Russian-Kyrgyz Development Fund financing. RackCorp markets international access to the facility (tenant/partner, not a separate facility).

name: iXAsia Datacenter Kyrgyzstan
notes: Operator official site (A) states Bishkek location, 3 MW, 300 racks (7-40 kW/rack), 1,600 sqm in three data halls, PUE < 1.4, Tier III claim (operator marketing; no independent Uptime certification record found), network-neutral colocation. Capacity/status per operator disclosure.

name: ProHost Data Center
notes: Operator page (A- for service offering) and Data Center Map directory (C) identify Data Center ProHost at Isa Akhunbayev St 119a, Bishkek with colocation/VPS/dedicated servers; operating since 2007 per HostDir. Facility-level power/racks specs not published; no MW capacity available.

name: KyrgyzTelecom ЦОД / DCASA co-location service
notes: Incumbent telecom official DCASA page (A) states co-location in KyrgyzTelecom data centres with power, conditioning and security (Bishkek plus regional telecom exchanges). Historical TAdviser/2017 Tier-III/5 MW concept is a B/C lead only; facility-level current specs not published.

name: Data Centre of the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic
developer: National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic
notes: Uptime Institute award record (A) confirms the NBKR data centre in Bishkek; Kabar state agency reported the president visited the Uptime-certified data processing centre in January 2020. Enterprise/central-bank facility, not colocation; public MW capacity not disclosed.

name: National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic Reserve Data Center
developer: National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic
notes: Uptime Institute lists a separate NBKR Reserve Data Center in Bishkek (A for asset existence); capacity and operational detail not public. Enterprise/central-bank DR facility.

name: State data processing centre (Государственный ЦОД) design project
developer: Ministry of Digital Development of the Kyrgyz Republic
notes: Official procurement record (A for tender, id 394299634, Aug 2023) plus Economist.kg/24.kg press (B) describe a design assignment for a state ЦОД of ~84.878m KGS, ~1,400 sqm, ~150 racks, likely Bishkek. Design/procurement stage only; no construction/commissioning evidence found - not counted as an operating facility.

name: Ministry of Internal Affairs (MIA) data centre procurement
developer: Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic
notes: Official procurement record (A) for a ministry data centre with installation/commissioning at Bishkek, pr. Ch. Aitmatova 95: 127,988,941 KGS planned amount, ~120-day delivery, DC/module/UPS/precision-cooling requirements (2026). Operational status requires acceptance/commissioning record; kept separate from the national/state-cloud ЦОД per KG methodology.

name: Green Data Center PPP project (ADB-supported)
developer: Government of the Kyrgyz Republic / PPP Center / Asian Development Bank
notes: ADB-supported PPP for design/financing/construction/O&M of a renewable-energy-powered green data centre near Bishkek; ADB consultant TOR (2025) and InfraPPP (B) report RFP July 2025 and feasibility/procurement support through Aug 2027. MW not disclosed; secondary sources cite ~300-500 racks. Site finalization around Bishkek; no construction evidence yet.

name: KG-IX / IX.KG internet exchange
notes: PeeringDB record (A) for KG-IX Bishkek: 22 peers, 29 connections, ~1.0 Tbps total capacity; KG-IX LLC at Razzakova 55, Bishkek (RIPE LIR). Internet exchange/interconnection facility at Bishkek, not a colocation data centre; recorded for interconnection completeness.

name: Ministry of Water Resources agricultural digital systems data center
developer: Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture and Processing Industry / KOICA
notes: Open.kg (C) reported a new data centre opened to support agricultural-sector digital information systems (livestock traceability) established with KOICA assistance (2025-12). Precise locality not disclosed; assigned to Bishkek because national ministries/digital platforms are based there - locality and MW capacity unverified.

name: Infocom / Тундук G-Cloud state e-government data processing infrastructure
notes: State e-services platform (Тундук) operated by Infocom (A for service operation); BGIR/Tunduk portal hosts a registry of data processing centres (ЦОД) including registered centres (e.g. id=37, launched 2010, 1,000,000 KGS cost), evidencing state data-processing infrastructure in Bishkek. Physical DC building details non-public; recorded as state e-gov/G-Cloud infrastructure per KG methodology.

name: Inspur Yunzhou Industrial Internet cooperation (MOU)
developer: Inspur Yunzhou Industrial Internet Co., Ltd (China) / Government of Kyrgyzstan
notes: Official digital.gov.kg post (2025) states an MOU covering digital technologies, construction of data-processing centres, cloud, AI and industrial internet (A for MOU intent only). No land, grid, construction, capacity or commissioning evidence found; recorded as announced/MOU lead, not a facility.

name: NSP Data Center (Network/Servers/Power colocation)
notes: RackCorp page (B) and NSP site describe a commercial colocation/cloud data centre in Chuy Region (Bishkek area), operator since 2003; Trend (B) reported the NSP-built facility opened Feb 2018 with 80 racks, 500 sqm, 300 kW initial electrical power expandable to 500 kW. Capacity recorded as 0.5 MW (electrical, per press); RackCorp markets international access.

name: Digital CASA traffic exchange / data center plan for Osh
developer: Government of the Kyrgyz Republic / World Bank Digital CASA program
notes: Kabar (2017) reported Digital CASA would build fibre and traffic-exchange centres including Bishkek, Osh and a data centre (~$10M component); AKIpress reported a presidential goal of one data centre per region announced at a forum in Osh. No public evidence of a completed physical data centre in Osh City; status kept planned, capacity unknown.

Method-driven sweep (2026-08-12): no verified physical data centre in Osh oblast outside Osh City. Regional ISPs (e.g. Eletcom in Nookat) and telecom exchanges are server rooms, not commercial DCs; Digital CASA traffic-exchange/data-centre plan is Osh City, not Osh oblast; no colocation/cloud customer evidence found.

Method-driven sweep (2026-08-12): no verified physical data centre in Jalal-Abad oblast. Energy towns (Tash-Kumyr) and mining-farm reports are leads without documented enterprise colocation/cloud customers; no official/operator/procurement facility evidence found.

Method-driven sweep (2026-08-12): no verified physical data centre in Batken oblast. Border/security region with essentially no DC pull factors per KG methodology; no state edge infrastructure, procurement or operator evidence found.

Method-driven sweep (2026-08-12): no verified physical data centre in Naryn oblast. Hydropower-cascade context only; university/campus and power-project hits without DC facility evidence; no procurement or operator records found.

Method-driven sweep (2026-08-12): no verified physical data centre in Talas oblast. Small economy with no DC pull factors; searches returned only general regional/telecom references; no facility evidence found.

Method-driven sweep (2026-08-12): no verified physical data centre in Issyk-Kul oblast. Karakol/Cholpon-Ata tourism-digital and event-infrastructure (F1H2O 2026) references surfaced but none constitutes a data-centre facility; no official/operator/procurement evidence found.
